newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha slumps, kerosene quiet despite cold.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha slumps, kerosene quiet despite cold.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices slumped on Wednesday, weighed down by overnight losses in the crude market and an easy supply/demand situation, traders said.
"Supplies are likely to be ample until early April, but should tighten afterwards," a trader said.
Open-spec naphtha second-half March was assessed at $228.50/230.50 and first-half April at $227.00/229.00 both down $2.00 from late Tuesday levels.
First-half April switched hands between Japanese traders at $229.00 on Tuesday, traders said. Spreads were stable with second-half March/second-half April at $3.00/4.00.

The kerosene market remained quiet with end-users seen relying largely on domestic barrels during February and March, traders said. They said the very low temperatures today, had not ignited buying interest.

Temperatures in Tokyo this morning were minus 0.6 degrees Celsius, down 9.1 C compared to Tuesday. The weather agency said the cold bite was expected to be brief with temperatures a little warmer next week.
There were rumours the last deal of February kerosene was made last week at about 35 cents above the mean of Singapore quotes on an FOB basis, but this could not be confirmed.
